name: Spastic Paraplegia-Precocious Puberty Syndrome
aliases: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia with Precocious Puberty

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Onset of secondary sexual characteristics before age 8 in females or 9 in males
MRI showing corticospinal tract abnormalities or spinal cord atrophy
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with hereditary spastic paraplegia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive lower limb spasticity combined with precocious puberty onset
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by neuroimaging and genetic testing when available

laboratory: Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels consistent with central precocious puberty
imaging: MRI showing corticospinal tract degeneration or spinal cord atrophy
Normal or nonspecific hypothalamic-pituitary region imaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes linked to hereditary spastic paraplegia (e.g., SPAST, ATL1)
other: Clinical observation of early pubertal development combined with progressive spasticity

distinguishingFeatures: No spasticity or corticospinal tract signs
Progressive neurological decline with adrenal insufficiency

redFlags: Rapid progression of lower limb spasticity
Early onset of puberty before age 8 (girls) or 9 (boys)
Emergence of bladder dysfunction or incontinence
references: Orphanet: Spastic paraplegia-precocious puberty syndrome, ORPHA:2826
Harding AE. Hereditary spastic paraplegias. Semin Neurol. 1993;13(4):333-342.
Carel JC, Leger J. Precocious puberty. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(22):2366-2377.
